medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Leave of absence, including the conditions and timing of the return, may be granted at the discretion of the dean.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: In the many medical specialty interest groups, students discuss professional goals and research interests. In service-oriented groups such as Prenatal Partners, Project Eye Care and the Global Health Coalition, they use their medical skills to serve others. In national groups like the American Medical Student Association, SALUD, Student National Medical Association, and Physicians for a National Health Plan, students connect with peers here and across the nation. And, with groups like the Running Club and intramural sports, students enjoy a well-earned break to both socialize and maintain their health. Through the student-run Health care, Education, and Active Living (HEALing) Clinics, student volunteers provide comprehensive primary care and social services to residents of Washington, DC's most underserved areas, regardless of insurance status or ability to pay. HEALing is the most expansive student-run clinic network in the region.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The School of Medicine and Health Sciences is on the Foggy Bottom campus of The George Washington University in Washington, DC. A subway stop sits immediately outside the medical school. The campus is within walking distance of the White House and the National Mall.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Some graduate student housing is available. The Washington, DC area has abundant off-campus housing options. For information, visit:  http://gwoffcampus.com/   Also, admitted students are invited to a formal "Second Look" in the spring before matriculation and housing resources are provided on that day.  In addition, accepted students join a private Facebook community that among other information provides housing tips as well as the ability to connect with future classmates regarding roommate possibilities.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Disability Support Services (DSS) is committed to providing equal educational opportunity and participation for all students at GW. DSS works to foster an environment that is inclusive and equitable by providing reasonable and appropriate accommodations and support services for students with disabilities.    https://disabilitysupport.gwu.edu/
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Collaborative student body who take advantage of a vibrant, urban campus in a city that has unparalleled opportunity for city, national and global connections.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: When relevant, guidance for appropriate attire in clinical settings may be provided.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: The Associate Dean for Student Affairs matches students with tutors from the fourth-year class and oversees the Big Sibling student mentoring program. Office hours are drop-in and by appointment.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Full clinical rotations begin in the month of March in the MS2 year.  Some patient interaction happens prior in the MS 1 year with Clinical Apprenticeship of CAP experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Weekly, several small-group sessions in addition to large-group lectures and three half days of independent study. Intersession allows students to integrate, consolidate, and reinforce their learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Required clerkships: Internal Med; Obstetrics/Gynecology; PEDS; Primary Care; Psychiatry; and Surgery.  Required advanced clerkships (i.e. emergency medicine, neurology, an acting internship) as well
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: Four-week, as a condition of admission, for a limited number of accepted students to preview first-year course content, meet student mentors, and attend skill workshops.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
Since 2014, the curriculum has: 
- Increased incorporation of active learning in place of traditional large-class lectures, which provides our students with an earlier clinical experience
- Enhanced professional development of students
- Integrated of material to enhance learning and retention
- Added independent study time
- Given additional focus on topics such as public health and clinical reasoning
- Provided incoming first-year students with an iPad
- Moved toward a paperless curriculum
- Begun Clinical clerkships begin in spring of second year
- Provided Multiple opportunities for students to explore career options in the full spectrum of medical specialties
- Offered unique only-in-Washington, D.C. educational experiences such as visiting Capitol Hill to learn about health care policy or visiting the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum to learn about medical ethics.

For more information see: http://smhs.gwu.edu/academics/md-program/curriculum
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: Several programs promoting primary care include:  the Clinical Apprenticeship Program (CAP) that matches first year students with clinical preceptors; the Community Urban Health Concentration; Longitudinal Primary Care Clinic; and the Interdisciplinary Student Community-Oriented Prevention Enhancement Service (ISCOPES) program. At the start of the Fundamentals of Clinical Practice, a month-long orientation will focus on enhancing clinical skills to prepare students for ward rotations. Throughout the Fundamentals of Clinical Practice, students will also participate in a Longitudinal Primary Care Clinic (LPCC) that complements our Primary Care Clerkship. Students will work one half-day every other week in a primary care setting regardless of their current rotation.  The GW Healing Clinic is a volunteer clinic operated by the students to provide primary care to the underserved patients  regardless of insurance status or ability to pay.  http://smhs.gwu.edu/healingclinic/
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Students have access to research opportunities at SMHS, the GW Cancer Institute and MFA as well as other leading health research organizations including Children's National Medical Center, the National Institutes of Health (NIH), and the Veterans Administration.  The areas of emphasis at SMHS are strategically targeted for programmatic growth and excellence. Key topics include neurodevelopmental disorders and autism, HIV/AIDS and neglected diseases of poverty, cardiovascular disease, stem cells, comparative effectiveness/patient outcomes, health policy and health disparities, and clinical trials. The School is investing significant resources into faculty recruitment and facilities upgrades to maintain and enhance the school's standing as a research-intensive institution. New NIH-funded state-of-the-art research laboratories support the Center for the Study of Neglected Diseases of Poverty.  See GW centers and institutes:  http://smhs.gwu.edu/research/centersinstitutes/index.html
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: In-depth structure and schedule information here:  http://smhs.gwu.edu/academics/md-program/curriculum/structure-and-schedule
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Students enjoy affiliated public and private community hospitals and the area's large military hospitals and facilities. See http://smhs.gwu.edu/academics/md-program/curriculum/affiliated-hospitals
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem: In Fundamentals of Medicine, students will be awarded a grade of Pass or Fail. In Fundamentals of Clinical Practice, students will be awarded a grade of Honors, High Pass, Pass, Conditional, or Fail.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: As the 11th oldest medical school in the country just a few blocks from the White House, we are positioned to influence health care locally, nationally, and globally.  In March of 2014, a new Clinical Learning and Simulation Skills (CLASS) Center, previously located in the hospital, opened within the School of Medicine in Ross Hall.  The new center in Ross Hall includes greater than 17,000 square feet of simulation, standardized patient, and learning / convening spaces.  The center includes:  centrally located control rooms, additional in- and out-patient rooms, debriefing rooms, wet and dry lab space, high-acuity simulation rooms using both standardized and simulated patients, administrative offices, and enhanced break out and storage space.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
The George Washington University School of Medicine and Health Sciences is dedicated to improving the health of our local, national, and global communities by:

Educating a diverse workforce of tomorrow's leaders in medicine, science, and health sciences.

Healing through innovative and compassionate care.

Advancing biomedical, translational, and health services delivery research with an emphasis on multidisciplinary collaboration.

Promoting a culture of excellence through inclusion, service, and advocacy.

As a globally recognized academic medical center, GW embraces the challenge of eliminating health disparities and transforming health care to enrich and improve the lives of those we serve.

medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
If the letter presented is a committee letter, (it can be one letter with no separate ones attached or it could be five or even more housed within the letter). 

If the approach is not a committee letter, the applicant must present at least 3 individual letters and the preference for the individual letter approach is that it not exceed five individual letters.   It is preferred that at least one of the letters be from a science faculty member. 

Please know that whatever number of letter(s) is indicated on an applicant's primary application as forthcoming, will be the number of letter(s) that need to be received for GW to view the file as complete from the perspective of recommendation letters.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Provided directly to all students who have been invited to interview.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Interviews are offered on a rolling basis and we typically interview from August through March.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Blind interviews (interviewer does not have access to interviewee's application file).
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Yes.  All interviews will be virtual until further notice.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Evaluated like US citizens and US Permanent residents.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: Must have US or Canadian undergraduate degree and non-private sponsorship in addition to other requirements.  https://smhs.gwu.edu/imp/programs/international-scholars/md-program-international-students
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: Must have or be about to earn a US or Canadian undergraduate degree.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: MCAT scores that include a score of 123 or below are considered non-competitive. We will continue to take the highest of each subsection across MCAT exams.   Further, in terms of subsection scores, generally, a 125 or greater is considered competitive for the Biological and Biochemical Foundations of Living Systems subsection.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: A cumulative GPA of below a 3.25 is considered non-competitive.   A science gpa below a 3.25 is considered non-competitive.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: The Committee on Admissions does accept coursework taken at a community college. However, it is preferable to have all of the premedical coursework taken at an accredited four-year college or university.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Once an applicant has a secondary application portal set up (after submission of the secondary), they may directly upload to their own portal any updates they choose to offer at any time in the process.   They should use this direct functionality alone and not email such updates.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo:
The faculty of the SMHS considers it essential for all medical graduates to have the knowledge
and skill to function in a variety of clinical situations and to provide a wide spectrum of patient
care as required by the curriculum. Therefore, every medical student must master a common
body of basic science knowledge and master the principles, knowledge, and procedures of the
core required disciplines. Fulfillment of the technical standards for graduation does not mean
the graduate will meet the technical standards of any residency program. This requires that
every student has sufficient capacities and abilities in:

Communication
Observation
Motor/tactile function
Emotions/Intellect
The MD degree is, thus, an undifferentiated degree requiring that each student independently demonstrate these capabilities. Surrogates cannot be used to accomplish the essential requirements. Students may not have undue dependence on technology or trained intermediaries.

medSchoolPrograms.info: "Early Selection" programs with numerous universities for second semester undergraduate sophomores interested in pursuing a GW M.D. degree.  Early Selection is a highly competitive program for applicants with academic distinction, a proven commitment to medicine with an early foundation in clinical experiences, and an interest in including more humanities, liberal arts and other non-science courses in their academic experience.  Please note that there are minimum eligibility requirements to apply which include a minimum overall 3.5 GPA and no Cs or below in science coursework. Students apply to the Early Selection program during the second semester of their sophomore year as an undergraduate. Current GW Applicants interested in Early Selection apply directly to the Office of Admissions, while those attending our contractual programs must be approved by a pre-medical advisor.  Please see:  http://smhs.gwu.edu/academics/md-program/admissions/joint-programs/early-selection

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec: With the development of AAMC/HHMI scientific and personal competencies, the George Washington University Committee on Admissions for the M.D. Program has moved from strict premedical requirements to competency-based recommendations. Mastery of these competencies should be reflected in strong academic performance, MCATs, experiences, and letters of reference.  For links to more information regarding recommendations, first visit our FAQ page:  http://smhs.gwu.edu/academics/md-program/admissions/faqs#coursework
medSchoolSelection.premedCourseworkNote: Note: This School has progressed to a competency-based admissions process.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: All coursework, regardless of age is accepted. However, the Committee on Admissions does recommend that you have completed some recent coursework .
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: The initial evaluation is based on data in the AMCAS and GW applications. This evaluation reviews academic performance; MCAT scores; extracurricular, health-related, research, and work experiences; evidence of non-scholastic accomplishments; and  examination of personal comments and letters of recommendation. The most promising applicants are invited for interview. The last phase includes the review by the Committee on Admissions of the entire dossier. This phase selects academically prepared students with personal characteristics and experiences the Committee considers important in future physicians.
